summary: - _(c) Direct the CTUIL to extend the last date of financial closure to 31.03.2027;_ - _(d) Pass any orders this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and equitable in favour of the Petitioner._ - _(a) Direct the CTUIL to not take any prejudicial/coercive steps for non-submissions of documents for financial closure in relation to Final Grant of Connectivity dated 28.08.2025 during the pendency of the present Petition._ - _(b) Pass any other order(s)/direction(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit in the interest of justice and equity._ f) Petitioner has referred to the Rajya Sabha discussion dated 29.07.2025, wherein it was stated that 43,922 MW of renewable power capacity for which LoAs had been issued by REIAs but PSAs with end-procurers had not been signed. - _“Learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the present Petition has been filed inter alia seeking extension of connectivity and corresponding Financial Closure milestone for the 700 MW Salgar Project being developed by the Petitioner at Solapur, Maharashtra. Learned counsel mainly submitted as under:_ - _(d) Subsequently, the Petitioner vide letter dated 18.2.2025 inter-alia requested CTUIL that, in view of the in-principle grant of connectivity, convey its approval on the revised connectivity dates. In response, CTUIL vide its e-mail dated 5.8.2025, requested the Petitioner to submit the documents of financial closure by 30.9.2025. (e) The Petitioner vide e-mail dated 21.8.2025, requested the CTUIL to issue a revised in-principle grant of connectivity along with the final grant of connectivity, with a revised date in view of the discussions held in the 38th CMETS Meeting held on 11.8.2025. Accordingly, the Petitioner requested an extension of the due date of submissions of financial closure. Despite the earlier-mentioned requests, on 28.8.2025, CTUIL proceeded to issue final connectivity, prescribing the start date of connectivity as 31.3.2026._ _(g) Since the trigger date in respect of the submission of Financial Closure documents falls on 30.9.2025, the Petitioner is pressing for an interim direction to CTUIL to not take any prejudicial/coercive steps for non-submissions of documents for financial closure in relation to the final grant of connectivity dated 28.8.2025 during the pendency of the present Petition._ _2. In response to the specific query of the Commission as to whether the Petitioner has acquired the required land for the project, the learned counsel submitted that the Petitioner has acquired 603 acres of land out of 2800 acres._ _3. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the Petitioner, the Commission directed that a notice be issued to the Respondent to file its reply.”_ - c) Order had been placed for 315 MVA 400/33 kV Power Transformer through its EPC Contractor for the Project, and a copy of the Purchase Order issued for the purchase of the Transformer. _"At the outset, the learned counsel for the Petitioner, WFEPL, highlighted that the Respondent, CTUIL, is yet to file its reply as per the direction vide Record of Proceedings dated 18.9.2025. Learned counsel further made detailed submissions as under:_ _(h) The Petitioner has already acquired 745 acres of land out of 2800 acres of land for the Project and will take some time to acquire the requisite amount of land; therefore, the start date of connectivity will be extended to 30.9.2026. Further, the trigger date in respect of the submission of Financial Closure documents falls on 30.9.2025; therefore, the Petitioner is also pressing for an interim direction to CTUIL to not take any prejudicial/coercive steps for nonsubmissions of documents for financial closure in relation to the final grant of connectivity dated 28.8.2025 during the pendency of the present Petition._ _3. After hearing the learned counsel for the parties, the Commission directed the CTUIL to file its reply along with the information called for vide RoP dated 18.9.2025 within two weeks, with a copy to the Petitioner, who may file its response thereof, within a week thereafter._ _4. The Commission directed the CTUIL to maintain the status quo till the next date of hearing.”_ - _“At the outset, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Respondent, CTUIL, had filed its reply only yesterday, and accordingly, the Petitioner may be granted two weeks’ time to file its rejoinder thereto._ _2. Considering the request of the learned counsel for the Petitioner, the Commission permitted the Petitioner to file its rejoinder to the Respondent, CTUIL’s reply, within two weeks. In the meantime, CTUIL shall maintain the status quo till the next date of hearing._ _“At the outset, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the parties have already argued the matter on previous hearings and hence, the matter may be reserved for order. The learned counsel for the Respondent/CTUIL, while agreeing to the above, also requested to reserve the matter for order._ _2. Considering the above, the Commission reserved the matter for order. The interim direction issued vide Record of Proceedings dated 24.2.2026 will continue until a decision is taken in the matter.”_ 12. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner, Respondent and perused the facts available on record. The following issue arises for our consideration: - **Whether any directions are required to be issued to extend the start date of connectivity of Petitioner’s project from 31.03.2026 to 30.09.2027 and consequential extension of the last date for achieving Financial Closure from 30.09.2025 to 31.03.2027?** 17. Petitioner has relied upon previous instances where an extension/ change in start date had been permitted in CMETS deliberations by the CTUIL. Petitioner has also referred to the relief granted by the Commission in relation to Financial Closure timelines.
title: Petition under Section 79(1)(c) and (f) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulation 41 and 42 of the CERC (Connectivity and General Network Access to the Inter-State Transmission System) Regulations, 2022 (as amended) seeking extension of connectivity start date and corresponding milestones (including financial closure) for the 700 MW Solar Power Project at Solapur, Maharashtra. 1.
